items.title: Secrets Unlocked: Evaluating LLMs for Secrets Detection in Android Apps
items.abstract: Mobile apps frequently embed sensitive secrets, such as API keys, access tokens, client secrets, and private keys that support internal functionality or enable integration with external systems and third-party services. Developers frequently embed these secrets into Android apps, which allows attackers to extract them through reverse engineering. Once exposed, attackers can exploit them to access sensitive data, manipulate resources, or abuse APIs, resulting in severe security and potential financial risks. In this paper, we present the first large-scale empirical evidence that off-the-shelf large language models (LLMs) can automatically identify secrets in Android apps without any domain-specific prior knowledge, thereby substantially lowering the barrier for attackers. On a benchmark of 5135 Android apps from prior work, LLMs rediscovered 93% of previously known secrets and identified 4361 additional valid credentials (+195%). Extending our analysis to 50 000 Google Play apps collected between August and October 2025, we conducted the largest-scale study to date on secret detection in Android apps, identifying secrets in 17 590 apps (35%). Among the 18 908 detected secrets, 1802 remained active at discovery, including, among others, critical credentials such as Stripe payment keys, OpenAI API keys, and GitHub personal access tokens. We responsibly contacted all the affected developers, of whom 170 confirmed the issues and updated their apps accordingly. Our findings empirically demonstrate the reality of vibe hacking: anyone can now leverage publicly accessible AI models to perform complex offensive security tasks with minimal expertise.

items.title: SEDIMA: Cross-Run Hierarchical Insight Memory for Evolutionary Search Agents
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven evolutionary search is a powerful paradigm for automated program and algorithm discovery, yet existing systems are largely memoryless: each run explores from scratch, so agents repeatedly rediscover the same improvements and re-encounter the same dead ends. We introduce SEDIMA, a persistent hierarchical insight memory for evolutionary search agents. SEDIMA distills raw traces into natural-language insights, clusters them by semantic similarity using attention-weighted centroids, and retrieves relevant guidance to condition future mutations, accumulating transferable knowledge across runs and problems rather than within a single trajectory. As a drop-in module that leaves the search operators unmodified, SEDIMA improves average final performance by 5.5% on AlgoTune and 6.6% on ALE-Bench LITE under a fixed budget of 100 evaluated candidates. Under OpenEvolve, SEDIMA requires 32.3% fewer iterations on average to reach baseline-best performance across the five evaluated backbones.

items.title: Self-Optimizing Multi-Agent Manufacturing Systems Using Hybrid Optimization and Intelligent Control Techniques
items.abstract: The increasing complexity and dynamic nature of modern manufacturing systems, driven by the Industry 4.0 and emerging Industry 5.0 paradigms, require intelligent, adaptive, and decentralized control frameworks. This paper proposes a novel Self-Optimizing Multi-Agent Manufacturing System (SOMAMS) that integrates multi-agent systems (MAS), hybrid optimization techniques, and intelligent control strategies into a unified architecture. The proposed framework adopts a layered design that combines supervisory coordination, hybrid Genetic Algorithm-Particle Swarm Optimization (GA-PSO), and reinforcement learning-based control to enable real-time, autonomous decision-making in distributed manufacturing environments. The system is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem aiming to minimize makespan, energy consumption, tardiness, and operational cost under practical manufacturing constraints. The hybrid GA-PSO algorithm enhances the speed of convergence and the quality of the solution by effectively balancing exploration and exploitation, while reinforcement learning enables agents to dynamically adapt to environmental changes. The decentralized agent-based structure supports scalable coordination among product, machine, and resource agents, facilitating self-organization and resilience. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in achieving rapid convergence, generating Pareto-like trade-offs between conflicting objectives, and maintaining balanced machine utilization. Additional analyzes, including scheduling visualization, learning performance, and agent interaction patterns, validate the system’s ability to optimize production efficiency while ensuring adaptability and robustness. The integration of cyber-physical systems and digital twin concepts further enables real-time monitoring and continuous self-optimization. In general, the proposed approach provides a comprehensive solution for next-generation smart manufacturing systems, offering significant improvements in flexibility, efficiency, and sustainability. The framework also establishes a foundation for future advancements in deep reinforcement learning and agentic artificial intelligence for fully autonomous industrial systems.
